title: Speed against momentum separates the hadrons
caption: At the same momentum a heavier particle is slower. At p = 0.5 GeV the pion has β = 0.963 and the proton β = 0.47, so the proton's dE/dx ∝ 1/β² is about 4× larger. By a few GeV all three have β near 1: dE/dx and time of flight lose their power, and Cherenkov detectors take over.
alt: Speed β against momentum for pion, kaon and proton: the three curves rise from zero and approach 1, the pion fastest and the proton slowest, with 0.963 and 0.470 marked at 0.5 GeV.
description: β = p/E = p/√(p² + m²), with m² = 0.0195, 0.244 and 0.880 GeV² for the pion, kaon and proton.
At p = 0.5 GeV: pion E = 0.519 GeV, β = 0.963; proton E = 1.063 GeV, β = 0.47.
dE/dx ∝ 1/β² makes the proton's loss about 4 times the pion's.
At high p every curve tends to β = 1.
